t.E1518.agn: In 1975 JECFA set the ADI as 'not specified'; when evaluating it as a flavouring substance in 2002 it saw no safety concern at current intake.
t.E1518.body: Triacetin is rapidly broken down in all tissues, including the digestive tract; it is absorbed from the gut faster than other fats and is used as an energy source.
t.E1518.found.1: Carrier in colour, flavouring and nutrient preparations (in flavourings, up to 3,000 mg/kg in food from all sources)
t.E1518.prod: Can be produced by heating glycerol with acetic anhydride or by a chemical reaction from allyl acetate and acetic acid.
t.E1518.regx.0: ADI 'not specified'; no safety concern as a flavouring substance.
t.E1518.summary: A humectant produced from glycerol and acetic acid. It is used in chewing gum and flavourings.
t.E1518.what: A humectant and carrier solvent formed by the full esterification of glycerol with acetic acid (triacetin).
